model_annotations.Bulgarian: This plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) output across different layers of a model, using a threshold of 1e-2, comparing three different conditions. The x-axis represents "Layer," displayed on a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 23, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis represents "Sparsity Ratio," also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The first line, shown in blue with a dashed line style, represents "sparsity ratio before gate" with an average of 0.03; it starts at approximately 0.18 at layer 0, drops quickly to around 0.04 by layer 3, and remains relatively flat and low throughout the remaining layers, ending near 0.0 at layer 23. The second line, shown in orange with a dotted line style, represents "sparsity ratio after gate" with an average of 0.44; it begins at approximately 1.0 at layer 0, decreases in a generally declining trend through the layers, reaching around 0.47 near layer 9, continuing to decline to approximately 0.15–0.20 around layers 14–16, and then fluctuating between roughly 0.10 and 0.40 in the later layers, ending near 0.30 at layer 23. The third line, shown in green with a dash-dot line style, represents "sparsity ratio after average gate" with an average of 0.33; it starts at approximately 0.95 at layer 0, declines steeply to about 0.45 by layer 7, continues decreasing to around 0.20 near layer 12, then remains relatively low between approximately 0.05 and 0.15 from layers 13 to 21, before showing a slight uptick to around 0.10 at layer 23.
